record.paper_title: Selection Principles and Special Sets of Reals
record.original_question: For sets of reals, is either of the Borel selection properties S1(BΩ, BΩ) or Sfin(BΩ, BΩ) hereditary, meaning inherited by every subset?

evidence.quote: Is S1(BΩ, BΩ) or Sfin(BΩ, BΩ) hereditary?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a separable metrizable space (e.g., a set of real numbers with the subspace topology). A family $\mathcal{U}$ of subsets of $X$ is called a cover of $X$ if $X = \bigcup \mathcal{U}$ and $X \notin \mathcal{U}$. A cover $\mathcal{U}$ of $X$ is called an $\omega$-cover if every finite subset of $X$ is contained in some single member of $\mathcal{U}$. Denote by $\mathcal{B}_\Omega$ the collection of all countable Borel $\omega$-covers of $X$ (covers consisting of Borel subsets of $X$).

For collections $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$ of covers of $X$, consider the following selection principles:
\begin{itemize}
  \item $S_1(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})$: For every sequence $(\mathcal{U}_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of elements of $\mathcal{A}$, there exist $U_n \in \mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\{U_n : n\in\mathbb{N}\} \in \mathcal{B}$.
  \item $S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{B})$: For every sequence $(\mathcal{U}_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of elements of $\mathcal{A}$, there exist finite sets $\mathcal{F}_n \subseteq \mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb{N}} \mathcal{F}_n \in \mathcal{B}$.
\end{itemize}

A property $P$ of separable metrizable spaces is said to be hereditary if whenever $X$ satisfies $P$, every subset of $X$ (with the subspace topology) also satisfies $P$.

Question: Is the property $S_1(\mathcal{B}_\Omega,\mathcal{B}_\Omega)$ hereditary for sets of real numbers? Is the property $S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{B}_\Omega,\mathcal{B}_\Omega)$ hereditary for sets of real numbers?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether $S_1(\mathcal{B}_\Omega,\mathcal{B}_\Omega)$ and $S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{B}_\Omega,\mathcal{B}_\Omega)$ are hereditary appears to remain open. Related work (e.g., Bartoszyński–Tsaban) studies hereditary versions of these classes and shows partial results (for example, that if $S_1(\mathcal{B}_\Omega,\mathcal{B}_\Omega)$ is preserved by finite powers it equals a hereditary class), but no full resolution of the heredity question itself has been found.

status_evidence.title: Hereditary topological diagonalizations and the Menger-Hurewicz Conjectures
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses hereditariness of topological diagonalization classes for Borel and open covers, including S_1(B_Ω,B_Ω) and S_fin(B_Ω,B_Ω).
status_evidence.claim: Hereditariness of these Borel ω-cover selection classes is studied as an open question, with partial results.

status_evidence.title: Some New Directions in Infinite-combinatorial Topology
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems on selection principles for Borel covers, including heredity questions for S_1(B_Ω,B_Ω) and S_fin(B_Ω,B_Ω).
status_evidence.claim: The heredity of these Borel ω-cover selection principles is listed among open problems.
